style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The only psalm the Psalter itself assigns to a day: 'a song for the Sabbath.' It is the psalm of the seventh day, and it does what Sabbath is for -- it stops working long enough to look at God's works. It is good to give thanks, to tell of covenant love in the morning and faithfulness at night, with the ten-string and the lyre. How great are Your works, LORD; how deep Your thoughts -- and the brute and the fool cannot see it, because the wicked flourish like grass and they mistake the grass for the forest. The psalm's answer is time: grass is destroyed forever; the LORD is on high forever. The enemies scatter; the psalmist's horn is lifted and he is anointed with fresh oil. Then the picture Sabbath exists to remind us of: the righteous flourish like the palm and grow like a cedar of Lebanon -- planted in the house of the LORD, still bearing fruit in old age, still full of sap and green -- to declare that the LORD is upright, my Rock, with no injustice in Him. A tree does not hurry; neither does the seventh day.

1.text: A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day. How good it is to give thanks to the LORD, and to make music to Your name, O Most High --
1.amp: A Psalm [mizmor] or Song [shir] for the sabbath [shabbath] day [yom]. It is a good [tov] thing to give thanks [yadah] unto the LORD [YHWH], and to sing praises [zamar] unto Your name [shem], O most High [Elyon]:
1.notes: shir le-yom ha-shabbat (H7892, H3117, H7676): the only psalm assigned by its own title to a day of the week. tov le-hodot la-YHWH (H2896, H3034): 'good' -- the Sabbath's own word from Genesis 2 -- to give thanks; u-le-zammer le-shimkha Elyon (H2167, H8034, H5945).

2.text: to tell of Your covenant love in the morning, and Your faithfulness through the nights,
2.amp: To show forth [nagad -- declare] Your lovingkindness [chesed -- covenant love] in the morning [boqer], and Your faithfulness [emunah] every night ['in the nights', layil, the KJV margin],
2.notes: le-haggid ba-boqer chasdekha (H5046, H1242, H2617): covenant love is the morning's news -- ve-emunatekha ba-lelot (H530, H3915): faithfulness is the nights' (plural), when it has to be believed rather than seen. The day framed by two attributes, the pattern of the morning and evening sacrifice.

3.text: on the ten-stringed instrument and on the lute, with a meditative strain on the lyre.
3.amp: Upon an instrument of ten strings [asor], and upon the psaltery [nebel -- lute]; upon the harp [kinnor -- lyre] with a solemn sound ['Higgaion', higgayon -- a murmuring, meditative strain, the KJV margin].
3.notes: ale-asor va-ale-nabel (H6218, H5035), the ten-string and the lute; ale higgayon be-khinnor (H1902, H3658): higgayon is the murmuring, meditating sound -- Psalm 9:16's 'Higgaion. Selah' -- so the Sabbath's music is thoughtful, not only loud.

4.text: For You have made me glad, O LORD, by what You have done; at the works of Your hands I ring out with joy.
4.amp: For You, LORD [YHWH], have made me glad [samach] through Your work [poal]: I will triumph [ranan -- ring out for joy] in the works [maaseh] of Your hands [yad].
4.notes: ki simmachtani YHWH be-phoolekha (H8055, H6467): gladness caused by God's DOING -- be-maase yadekha arannen (H4639, H3027, H7442). The Sabbath is the day for admiring the Craftsman's work instead of adding to one's own (cf. Genesis 2:2-3).

5.text: How great are Your works, O LORD! Your thoughts run very deep.
5.amp: O LORD [YHWH], how great [gadal] are Your works [maaseh]! and Your thoughts [machashabah -- plans, designs] are very [meod] deep [amaq].
5.notes: mah-gadelu maasekha YHWH (H1431, H4639): the exclamation of Psalm 104:24 -- meod amequ machshevotekha (H3966, H6009, H4284): Your thoughts are VERY DEEP -- the plans behind the works, which the next verse says some people cannot fathom at all.

6.text: A brutish man does not know this, and a fool does not understand it:
6.amp: A brutish [baar -- dull as cattle] man [ish] knows [yada] not; neither does a fool [kesil -- dullard] understand [bin -- discern] this.
6.notes: ish-baar lo yeda (H376, H1198, H3045): the baar is the man with a beast's mind, Psalm 73:22's word for Asaph before he went into the sanctuary -- u-khesil lo-yavin et-zot (H3684, H995): the kesil, the thick-headed. 'This' is what follows: the law of grass.

7.text: when the wicked sprout up like grass and all the workers of iniquity blossom, it is so that they may be destroyed forever.
7.amp: When the wicked [rasha] spring [parach -- sprout, blossom] as the grass [eseb], and when all the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven] do flourish [tsuts -- bloom]; it is that they shall be destroyed [shamad -- annihilated] for ever [ad]:
7.notes: bi-phroach reshaim kemo eseb (H6524, H7563, H6212): the wicked sprouting like grass after rain -- va-yatsitsu kol-poale aven (H6692, H6466, H205), all the evildoers in bloom -- le-hishamedam ade-ad (H8045, H5703): the blossoming is the prelude to destruction, the way grass is greenest just before the scythe. Psalm 37:2 and 73:18-19 make the same argument.

8.text: But You, O LORD, remain exalted on high forever.
8.amp: But You, LORD [YHWH], are most high [marom -- on high, exalted] for evermore [olam].
8.notes: ve-attah marom le-olam YHWH (H4791, H5769): the shortest verse in the psalm and its center of gravity -- grass is destroyed ade-ad (v. 7); the LORD is high le-olam. Time is the answer to the fool's confusion.

9.text: For look -- Your enemies, O LORD, look, Your enemies will perish; all the workers of iniquity will be scattered.
9.amp: For, lo, Your enemies [oyeb], O LORD [YHWH], for, lo, Your enemies shall perish [abad]; all the workers [paal] of iniquity [aven] shall be scattered [parad -- separated, dispersed].
9.notes: ki hinneh oyevekha YHWH, ki-hinneh oyevekha yovedu (H341, H6): the doubled 'behold' of amazement -- yitparedu kol-poale aven (H6504, H6466, H205): the evildoers who bloomed together in verse 7 are scattered apart. Ugaritic poetry uses this same staircase repetition; the Sabbath psalm is old.

10.text: But You have lifted my horn high like the horn of the wild ox; I am anointed with fresh oil.
10.amp: But my horn [qeren] shall You exalt [rum] like the horn of an unicorn [reem -- the wild ox]: I shall be anointed [balal -- mingled, moistened] with fresh [raanan -- green, fresh] oil [shemen].
10.notes: va-tarem ki-reem qarni (H7311, H7214, H7161): the horn -- strength and dignity -- raised like the reem's, the wild aurochs, the most formidable animal Israel knew (the KJV's 'unicorn'). balloti be-shemen raanan (H1101, H8081, H7488): drenched with fresh oil -- the anointing of a guest of honor, and of a king.

11.text: My eye has looked upon those who lie in wait for me; my ears have heard the fate of the evildoers who rise against me.
11.amp: Mine eye [ayin] also shall see [nabat -- look upon] my desire on mine enemies [shur -- those who watch for me, lie in wait], and mine ears [ozen] shall hear [shama] my desire of the wicked [raa -- evildoers] that rise up [qum] against me.
11.notes: va-tabbet eni be-shurai (H5027, H5869, H7790): my eye has looked on my watchers -- shur, the ambusher's word -- and the ears shama (H241, H8085) about the mereim (H7489) who qum (H6965) against me. 'My desire' is the KJV's supplied object; the Hebrew just says he saw and heard -- the outcome of verse 9 witnessed.

12.text: The righteous will flourish like the palm tree; he will grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon.
12.amp: The righteous [tsaddiq] shall flourish [parach -- blossom] like the palm tree [tamar]: he shall grow [sagah -- grow great] like a cedar [erez] in Lebanon [Lebanon].
12.notes: tsaddiq ka-tamar yiphrach (H6662, H8558, H6524): the same parach as the wicked's grass (v. 7) -- but a palm, not a lawn: fruit-bearing, deep-rooted, tall. ke-erez ba-Lebanon yisgeh (H730, H3844, H7685): the cedar, the longest-lived tree Israel knew. Grass sprouts in a week; a cedar takes a century -- the Sabbath-view of growth.

13.text: Those transplanted into the house of the LORD will blossom in the courtyards of our God.
13.amp: Those that be planted [shathal -- transplanted] in the house [bayith] of the LORD [YHWH] shall flourish [parach] in the courts [chatser] of our God [Elohim].
13.notes: shetulim be-bet YHWH (H8362, H1004): shathal is TRANSPLANTED -- Psalm 1:3's tree 'planted by the rivers' is this same verb: moved by a gardener to good ground. be-chatsrot Elohenu yaphrichu (H2691, H430, H6524): the courtyard of God's house as the soil the righteous grow in.

14.text: They will still be bearing fruit in old age; they will stay full of sap and green,
14.amp: They shall still bring forth fruit [nub] in old age [sebah -- gray-headed age]; they shall be fat [dashen -- juicy, full of sap] and flourishing ['green', raanan, the KJV margin];
14.notes: od yenuvun be-sebah (H5107, H7872): STILL fruiting in gray-headed age -- deshenim ve-raanannim yihyu (H1879, H7488): sap-full and green, the same raanan as the fresh oil of verse 10. The psalm's promise to the old: rootedness in God does not dry out (cf. Isaiah 46:4).

15.text: to declare that the LORD is upright -- my Rock, and there is no injustice in Him.
15.amp: To show [nagad -- declare] that the LORD [YHWH] is upright [yashar]: He is my rock [tsur], and there is no unrighteousness [avlah -- injustice, wrong] in Him.
15.notes: le-haggid ki-yashar YHWH (H5046, H3477): the fruitful old are a DECLARATION -- the same nagad as verse 2's morning and night telling -- that the LORD is straight-dealing. tsuri ve-lo-avlatah bo (H6697, H5766): my Rock, and no crookedness in Him: Deuteronomy 32:4's Rock, sung on the seventh day. The fool of verse 6 said the grass proved otherwise; the cedar answers him.
